title: Use defined() with quotes, they're not optional.
issue_title: Improper use of `defined` to check for a constant
issue_body:
<!--
****************************
DO NOT disclose security issues here, contact security@prestashop.com instead!
****************************
-->

#### Describe the bug

`defined(_CONSTANT_)` is wrong. Quotes are not optional.

    var_dump(defined('_CONSTANT_'));  // false
    var_dump(defined(_CONSTANT_));  // false
    define('_CONSTANT_', true);
    var_dump(defined('_CONSTANT_'));  // true
    var_dump(defined(_CONSTANT_));  // false (INCORRECT)
    // Warning:  Use of undefined constant _CONSTANT_ - assumed '_CONSTANT_' (this will throw an Error in a future version of PHP)

#### Expected behavior

The PHP function `defined()` should always be used with quotes when testing for a literal constant.

#### Additional information

This error occurs 6 times in `Prestashop/Prestashop`, and once in `Prestashop/pagesnotfound`.
Two occurrences in `Prestashop/Prestashop` fixed in #24985
Four occurrences in `Prestashop/Prestashop` fixed in #25003 
Occurrence in `Prestashop/pagesnotfound` fixed in https://github.com/PrestaShop/pagesnotfound/pull/15#issue-672656650

  • The `Tab` structure changed and 2 new fields (`wording` & `wording_domain`) have been added but are not present yet when migrating the tab in the 1.7.0.0.sql script file. Unsetting those 2 keys from the data array solve this issue
  • `$this->translator->getSourceString()` could return an `int` in some cases, breaking the return type and leading to an exception. Casting the returned value to `string` solve the issue

title: When saving an image as a square png, add always a transparent border
issue_title: Using `png_all` option in BO, all images should have transparent background in FO
issue_body:
#### Describe the bug

This is somewhere between a bug and an improvement.

When choosing `Use PNG for all images` (`png_all`) as Image format (in menu *Design - Image Settings*), the background is transparent when the original image is in png format and white otherwise.

#### Steps to reproduce
1. Use these two images. [test_images.zip] One is in png format, and one is in jpg format (https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/files/6279138/test_images.zip)
2. In menu *Improve - Design - Image Settings*, under *Image generation options*
    for *Image format* choose *Use PNG for all images*
    for *Generate images based on one side of the source image* choose *Automatic (longest size)*
3. Upload both images into a product.
4. Go to the image folder and inspect the generated images.

#### Observed behavior
The resulting resized images are different. Even though they are both saved as png, one is transparent and the other is not (the added border is white, when the original file was in jpg format, and it is transparent when the original was in png format.
a) The original was jpg. The result is a png with a white border (`cart_default` size).
![62673-cart_default](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7520695/115393433-faa89d80-a1e1-11eb-8fbd-df532c7537fe.jpg)
b) The original was png. The result is a png with a transparent border (`cart_default` size).
![83771-cart_default](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7520695/115393505-114ef480-a1e2-11eb-874d-ac3aa101ac25.jpg)
Change github.com to dark mode to see the difference immediately. Or see below https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/23920#issuecomment-822564239 for a screenshot.

#### Expected behavior
I expect both images to be visually the same, with a transparent border. The output format is png for both, because we 
have choosen *Use PNG for all images* (`png_all`), therefore both should have a transparent border.

This would allow for more flexibility for the design of the templates. Also it makes more sense to always make use of the advantages the png format offers when we choose *Use PNG for all images* (`png_all`), and not make the use of transparency dependent on the source format.

#### Backwards compatibility

This should be backwards compatible, since images whose original format is png are already transparent.
It removes the constraint that a template must give a white background to the image in order to hide the difference between a jpg and a png image.

#### Additional information

* PrestaShop version: 1.6.1.1 and 1.7.7.3
* PHP version: any

issue_body: **Describe the bug** It should not be possible to purchase a pack which requires more quantity of pack item than there is in stock. **To Reproduce** In Admin I have pack product. In that Pack product I have added a combination product with quantity 100. The combination product itself has less than 100 quantity availability (for example, 99). Global setting for packs is to "Decrease both". My Global Availability preference is "Deny orders" when out of stock. _Result_: It is possible to add to cart and purchase the pack. This results in my combination product having a negative quantity after the purchase. title: Fixed API inconsistent return format of JSON
issue_title: API /orders endpoint inconsistent return format of JSON
issue_body:
#### Describe the bug

Endpoint /orders have 2 different formats of json returned based on quantity of orders which will be fetched.

#### Expected behavior

I expect it to returns orders in same format, or different HTTP status code for empty list. The first one is a preffered

#### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Call api /orders?output_format=JSON&display=full
2. It will be in format
`{
    "orders": [
        {
        ...
}
]}`
3. Call api /orders?output_format=JSON&display=full&limit=100000,20 (or other limit number which will return empty list)
4. Response will be in format
`[]`

That format is wrong, if you look at xml response you can see that it always returns format
```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<prestashop xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">
    <orders></orders>
</prestashop>
```

Preffered format of json for empty list of orders should be like this:
```
{
    "orders": []
}
```
Now you clearly see that base object is an Object not a List/Array of objects and that orders are empty
